claims.text: The initial FeCoNi high-entropy alloy is single-phase fcc.
Introducing a secondary phase into single-phase fcc FeCoNi-based alloys will increase coercivity.
Refining the grains of single-phase fcc FeCoNi-based alloys will increase coercivity.
A secondary phase raises coercivity by pinning magnetic domain walls.
The coercive field of the single-phase fcc FeCoNi baseline is no greater than 100 Oe.
The modified material will have higher coercivity than single-phase fcc FeCoNi or a corresponding derivative.
The magnitude of the coercivity increase may depend on the identity of the secondary phase.
The magnitude of the coercivity increase may depend on the grain-size distribution.
The target structural boundary is an fcc FeCoNi-based alloy with either secondary phases or refined grains.
Coercivity will be evaluated from room-temperature magnetic hysteresis measurements.
The experiment will compare FeCoNi-based alloys having varied secondary-phase content or grain size.
Failure to observe a coercive field above 100 Oe after either modification will falsify the hypothesis.

contradictions.description: The prediction is any increase relative to the baseline, whereas the falsification rule uses 100 Oe without clearly stating whether this is an absolute coercivity threshold or an increase of 100 Oe. A relative increase could therefore satisfy the prediction while still meeting the stated falsification condition.
